election._doc: Facts about one federal general election that aren't in FEC data, entered by hand once per cycle (see design/races/README.md, 'Each cycle'). The races step reads this to build data/races-<year>.json.
election.lateGeneralNote: The day after the last regular primary (Sept. 15). General-election money given from here on can only go to a nominee.
election.houseSeatsNote: House seats per state (the 2020 census apportionment, for 2022–2030); a state with one seat elects it at large. Races for seats outside this are stray filings and are dropped.

states.AL: The Supreme Court let Alabama return to its 2023 congressional map on June 2, 2026, with special primaries in the districts that changed.
states.CA: California voters approved new congressional maps (Proposition 50) on Nov. 4, 2025.
states.FL: Florida enacted new congressional maps on May 4, 2026.
states.LA: Louisiana enacted new congressional maps on May 29, 2026.
states.NC: North Carolina enacted new congressional maps on Oct. 22, 2025.
states.OH: Ohio adopted new congressional maps on Oct. 31, 2025.
states.TN: Tennessee adopted new congressional maps on May 7, 2026.
states.TX: Texas enacted new congressional maps in August 2025.
states.UT: Utah's congressional maps were redrawn by court order on Nov. 10, 2025.

systemNotes.louisiana: Louisiana held its open House primary on Nov. 3, with every party on one ballot; where no one won a majority, the top two meet in a runoff on Dec. 12.

senateSpecials.OH: a special election for the rest of JD Vance's term, through January 2029
senateSpecials.FL: a special election for the rest of Marco Rubio's term, through January 2029

election.certificationNote: When each state certifies (by statute or its published calendar; null where it isn't posted) and where its official results are, for `pnpm race-results status`. Gathered Nov. 16, 2026 from official sites; check each cycle.
